purpose: Prove Multi team capability actually runs a collaboration loop with a real model. Not a Terminal-Bench score, and not a claim that Multi is better on hard work.

scope_limits.notes: The fixture states the finding outright and the instruction prescribes which tools to call in which order, so gate 1 answers 'does the team machinery actually fire end to end under a real model', not 'does Multi help on a task with real analysis'. Deliberate: decision 010 froze this carrier because a single-operator task lets the model finish alone and never touch a team tool, which would fail gate 1 for task difficulty rather than for a product defect. The WBS phrase 'full collaboration semantics on a real task' is only satisfied by gate 1 and gate 2 read together: gate 1 supplies the collaboration evidence, gate 2 supplies the real tasks. Neither gate alone may be quoted as satisfying it.
scope_limits.gate2_order_bias: base_order runs Codex before Multi on every task, so Multi inherits a warmed image. That bias favours Multi, and gate 2 only calls degradation when Codex completes and Multi does not, so it makes the degradation verdict more conservative rather than fabricating one. It does weaken a 'no degradation observed' reading.

finding_line: M5-COLLAB-FINDING: orders.legacy_total is dropped by migration 0042

evidence_source.wait_signal: Wait completed: the team world state changed. The current active view is in this request.
evidence_source.notes: Judge reads harness-captured Responses function_call_output (loopback/budget-proxy request bodies). codex exec --json does not emit team_inspect payloads and wait items omit the TeamActivity message. TEAM_REPORT is never collaboration evidence. Same-snapshot dump pages concatenate when the call has a cursor; a dump without a cursor replaces. Every row is attributed to the producing call: only team_inspect output yields dump/log rows and only wait_agent output yields a wake signal, so a payload echoed by another tool cannot manufacture a pass. Verified wire shape on the frozen binary: plain name plus namespace=collaboration, CLI-written output.

collaboration_predicates.description: Root spawned exactly one member. Dump has a non-root participant.
The selected Event has two or more Versions.
Those Versions on the same Event were written by at least two distinct authors, including the member.
A route assignment on that Event targets the member.
A member-authored Version on that Event is evidence-backed.
Root set root_state=resolved on a member-authored Version of that Event.
Harness evidence shows Root was woken: team_inspect log signalled a Root wake, or wait_agent returned the TeamActivity message.
